{"parentUuid":"1f7b251f-da9b-4094-8d0b-6942de6969c8","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfWyeqnveGrdQJzH2FtF2","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01MZmvJ4pwETTdH24geSvMmv","name":"Edit","input":{"replace_all":false,"file_path":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/notes/client-brief.md","old_string":"## Confirmed decisions (2026-09-28)\n\n- **Publishing is admin-only.** Only the manager/admin role can publish content live;\n  editors can create and edit drafts but cannot move them to *published*. This resolves\n  the \"exact roles\" open question below for the publish action specifically — it settles\n  who can flip status, not yet the full list of what else an editor can/can't touch.\n- **Homepage priority order: address, hours, directions first.** This confirms and\n  narrows the \"one glance\" framing above — of the \"what/where/when\" facts a first-time\n  visitor needs, address/hours/directions rank above signature-dish or walk-in-only copy\n  on the homepage specifically (those still belong on the page, just not the top fold).\n- **Contact method is phone only.** No contact form, no email address surfaced to\n  customers — a phone number is the one channel offered for reaching the restaurant.\n\n## Still open (proposed requirements to settle in `/grill-with-docs`, not decided here)\n\n- The rest of the admin/editor permission boundary beyond publishing (e.g. can an editor\n  manage users, change hours/menu content, or delete posts)\n- Whether \"News\" posts should be seeded with any real content (e.g. a real, dated,\n  citable event like the Michelin ceremony) vs. only demo placeholders\n- How to handle the site acknowledging \"also known as La Once Mil\" without confusing readers","new_string":"## Confirmed decisions (2026-09-28, in `/grill-with-docs`)\n\n- **Site display name is \"La Once Mil\"** — the restaurant's own verified branding.\n  (Corrects the earlier \"Tacos La Oncemil\" spelling used when this brief was started;\n  that was not an intentional name choice. See `notes/restaurant-research.md`.)\n- **Publishing is admin-only.** Only the manager/admin role can publish content live;\n  the demo editor can create and edit announcement drafts but cannot publish, cannot\n  edit permanent pages (Menu, Visit Us/Hours, Our Story), and cannot manage users. The\n  admin can do everything. This is a class prototype modeling a hypothetical future\n  hire, not real restaurant staff.\n- **Demo accounts are fictional, not the real owner.** Seed users are named\n  **\"Demo Manager\"** (admin) and **\"Demo Editor\"** (editor) — required to demonstrate\n  both roles for grading, but explicitly not claiming to be César de la Parra or any\n  real staff member.\n- **Homepage priority order: address, hours, directions first.** Of the \"what/where/when\"\n  facts a first-time visitor needs, address/hours/directions rank above signature-dish\n  or walk-in-only copy on the homepage specifically (those still belong on the page,\n  just not the top fold).\n- **Contact method is phone only.** No contact form, no email address surfaced to\n  customers — a phone number is the one channel offered for reaching the restaurant.\n- **Menu is one ordinary Markdown page** (dish names and descriptions), not a\n  structured menu/pricing database. No unverified peso prices are included, per\n  `notes/restaurant-research.md`'s pricing caveat.\n- **News/announcements may include one real, dated item** — the Michelin star\n  announcement, since the Michelin Guide page directly confirms the exact distinction\n  (\"One MICHELIN Star\") and attributes it to the Lomas de Chapultepec address\n  specifically (see `notes/restaurant-research.md`). Any other seed announcements are\n  invented sample content and must be clearly labeled as demo, not real restaurant\n  posts.\n- **Images: placeholders now, real photos intended for the final version.** Build\n  proceeds today with clearly labeled placeholders (e.g. `[PLACEHOLDER: storefront\n  photo]`) so nothing blocks on photo access. See \"Image tracker\" below for what's\n  still needed before final.\n\n## Image tracker (placeholders in use until these are supplied)\n\n| Needed for | Status | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Homepage hero image | Placeholder | Storefront or signature dish shot, Lomas de Chapultepec location only |\n| Menu page image(s) | Placeholder | Food shots; no prices, per pricing caveat |\n| Our Story image | Placeholder | Chef/kitchen or storefront shot |\n| News/announcement images (optional, per post) | Placeholder | Only if a specific post needs one |\n\nPer `notes/restaurant-research.md`: the three photos found in the Michelin article are\ncredited \"© La Once Mil\" (editorial credit, not a republishing license) and are **not\ncleared for use**. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"ed761f93-07e5-49ef-9acc-4ce2c56076e2","timestamp":"2026-09-29T02:55:49.033Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/notes/client-brief.md","oldString":"## Confirmed decisions (2026-09-28)\n\n- **Publishing is admin-only.** Only the manager/admin role can publish content live;\n  editors can create and edit drafts but cannot move them to *published*. This resolves\n  the \"exact roles\" open question below for the publish action specifically — it settles\n  who can flip status, not yet the full list of what else an editor can/can't touch.\n- **Homepage priority order: address, hours, directions first.** This confirms and\n  narrows the \"one glance\" framing above — of the \"what/where/when\" facts a first-time\n  visitor needs, address/hours/directions rank above signature-dish or walk-in-only copy\n  on the homepage specifically (those still belong on the page, just not the top fold).\n- **Contact method is phone only.** No contact form, no email address surfaced to\n  customers — a phone number is the one channel offered for reaching the restaurant.\n\n## Still open (proposed requirements to settle in `/grill-with-docs`, not decided here)\n\n- The rest of the admin/editor permission boundary beyond publishing (e.g. can an editor\n  manage users, change hours/menu content, or delete posts)\n- Whether \"News\" posts should be seeded with any real content (e.g. a real, dated,\n  citable event like the Michelin ceremony) vs. only demo placeholders\n- How to handle the site acknowledging \"also known as La Once Mil\" without confusing readers","newString":"## Confirmed decisions (2026-09-28, in `/grill-with-docs`)\n\n- **Site display name is \"La Once Mil\"** — the restaurant's own verified branding.\n  (Corrects the earlier \"Tacos La Oncemil\" spelling used when this brief was started;\n  that was not an intentional name choice. See `notes/restaurant-research.md`.)\n- **Publishing is admin-only.** Only the manager/admin role can publish content live;\n  the demo editor can create and edit announcement drafts but cannot publish, cannot\n  edit permanent pages (Menu, Visit Us/Hours, Our Story), and cannot manage users. The\n  admin can do everything. This is a class prototype modeling a hypothetical future\n  hire, not real restaurant staff.\n- **Demo accounts are fictional, not the real owner.** Seed users are named\n  **\"Demo Manager\"** (admin) and **\"Demo Editor\"** (editor) — required to demonstrate\n  both roles for grading, but explicitly not claiming to be César de la Parra or any\n  real staff member.\n- **Homepage priority order: address, hours, directions first.** Of the \"what/where/when\"\n  facts a first-time visitor needs, address/hours/directions rank above signature-dish\n  or walk-in-only copy on the homepage specifically (those still belong on the page,\n  just not the top fold).\n- **Contact method is phone only.** No contact form, no email address surfaced to\n  customers — a phone number is the one channel offered for reaching the restaurant.\n- **Menu is one ordinary Markdown page** (dish names and descriptions), not a\n  structured menu/pricing database. No unverified peso prices are included, per\n  `notes/restaurant-research.md`'s pricing caveat.\n- **News/announcements may include one real, dated item** — the Michelin star\n  announcement, since the Michelin Guide page directly confirms the exact distinction\n  (\"One MICHELIN Star\") and attributes it to the Lomas de Chapultepec address\n  specifically (see `notes/restaurant-research.md`). Any other seed announcements are\n  invented sample content and must be clearly labeled as demo, not real restaurant\n  posts.\n- **Images: placeholders now, real photos intended for the final version.** Build\n  proceeds today with clearly labeled placeholders (e.g. `[PLACEHOLDER: storefront\n  photo]`) so nothing blocks on photo access. See \"Image tracker\" below for what's\n  still needed before final.\n\n## Image tracker (placeholders in use until these are supplied)\n\n| Needed for | Status | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Homepage hero image | Placeholder | Storefront or signature dish shot, Lomas de Chapultepec location only |\n| Menu page image(s) | Placeholder | Food shots; no prices, per pricing caveat |\n| Our Story image | Placeholder | Chef/kitchen or storefront shot |\n| News/announcement images (optional, per post) | Placeholder | Only if a specific post needs one |\n\nPer `notes/restaurant-research.md`: the three photos found in the Michelin article are\ncredited \"© La Once Mil\" (editorial credit, not a republishing license) and are **not\ncleared for use**. Real photos must come from the user's own Instagram pulls (with\npost date/caption/credit noted) or the user's own photography — not these Michelin\narticle images, and not AI-generated or stock substitutes.\n\n## Still open (proposed requirements to settle in `/grill-with-docs`, not decided here)\n\n- Whether \"Visit Us\" is its own page (separate from the homepage) or folded into Home","originalFile":"# Client brief: Tacos La Oncemil (La Once Mil), Lomas de Chapultepec, Mexico City\n\n## Why this client\n\nI picked this restaurant because the Michelin-star story is compelling: a taqueria — a\ncategory of restaurant normally associated with cheap, fast street food — won a Michelin\nstar in 2026, the only taquería to hold that distinction. That tension (a $20 wagyu taco next\nto a genre built on $1 street tacos) is a strong hook for a \"what can I eat here, where is it,\nwhen is it open\" public site, and the restaurant's real story (chef César de la Parra\ndeliberately elevating a street-food format he grew up on) gives the \"Our Story\" page\nsomething specific to say instead of generic restaurant copy.\n\n**Scope note:** this project models only the flagship location — Monte Everest 780, Lomas\nde Chapultepec — the Michelin-starred address. The restaurant also operates a second Mexico\nCity branch (Roma Norte) and, as of very recently (Sept 2026), a Madrid location; both are\nexplicitly out of scope. See `notes/restaurant-research.md` for full sourcing and the\nnaming decision (site uses \"Tacos La Oncemil,\" the restaurant's own primary branding is \"La\nOnce Mil\" — the two names are used interchangeably in the restaurant's own material).\n\n## Who runs the site, and how comfortable are they with computers?\n\n**Proposed assumption, not a verified fact** (I have not contacted the restaurant): the site\nis modeled as run by the owner, César de la Parra, posting everything himself. He's a working\nchef running a 55-seat, ~80-staff restaurant — comfortable enough to run Instagram and\nTikTok accounts personally, but with no patience for a complicated publishing workflow. He\nneeds to post fast between service, not fight with a CMS. This means the editor UI has to be\nsimple even though, today, there's only one real user.\n\nThe CMS still needs two enforced roles (admin/editor) per the assignment's fixed\nrequirements — the brief models a plausible future where a manager or social-media hire gets\nan editor account without touching user management, menu changes, or the ability to delete\nthe Visit Us / hours information.\n\n## Who reads it, and what are they usually trying to find?\n\nTwo kinds of visitors, inferred from the restaurant's real profile (no reservations, walk-in\nonly, high foot traffic from the Michelin attention, no functioning official website today):\n\n- **First-time visitors drawn by the Michelin coverage**, wanting to know: what's the\n  signature dish, what does it cost, where exactly is it, when is it open, is a reservation\n  needed (no).\n- **Repeat/local visitors** wanting quick answers: today's hours, any seasonal menu news,\n  confirmation the place hasn't moved.\n\n## What's broken about how they do it now?\n\nVerified from research: the restaurant has no functioning official website (`laoncemil.com`\nexists but shows only \"under construction\"). Its entire online presence is Instagram,\nTikTok, and a Linktree — none of which answer \"where and when\" quickly, and all of which bury\nthat information under a scrolling feed. Someone who doesn't already follow the account has\nno fast way to get the address and hours without digging through an Instagram bio.\n\n## What would make them say \"this is better\"?\n\nA page that says, in one glance: what the signature dishes are, that it's walk-in only\n(setting the right expectation before someone shows up expecting to book), the exact address\nand hours, and a way to see it's a real, currently-open, currently-relevant place (recent\nannouncements) without needing to already follow the Instagram.\n\n## What must not happen\n\n**This site must never imply that Tacos La Oncemil / La Once Mil commissioned, endorsed, or\nwas involved in building this project.** It is a student prototype built for a class\nassignment using publicly available, verified information. Any demonstration content (sample\nannouncements, seed data) must be clearly labeled as such, not presented as if the restaurant\nposted it.\n\n## Confirmed decisions (2026-09-28)\n\n- **Publishing is admin-only.** Only the manager/admin role can publish content live;\n  editors can create and edit drafts but cannot move them to *published*. This resolves\n  the \"exact roles\" open question below for the publish action specifically — it settles\n  who can flip status, not yet the full list of what else an editor can/can't touch.\n- **Homepage priority order: address, hours, directions first.** This confirms and\n  narrows the \"one glance\" framing above — of the \"what/where/when\" facts a first-time\n  visitor needs, address/hours/directions rank above signature-dish or walk-in-only copy\n  on the homepage specifically (those still belong on the page, just not the top fold).\n- **Contact method is phone only.** No contact form, no email address surfaced to\n  customers — a phone number is the one channel offered for reaching the restaurant.\n\n## Still open (proposed requirements to settle in `/grill-with-docs`, not decided here)\n\n- The rest of the admin/editor permission boundary beyond publishing (e.g. can an editor\n  manage users, change hours/menu content, or delete posts)\n- Whether \"News\" posts should be seeded with any real content (e.g. a real, dated,\n  citable event like the Michelin ceremony) vs. only demo placeholders\n- How to handle the site acknowledging \"also known as La Once Mil\" without confusing readers\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":65,"oldLines":23,"newStart":65,"newLines":55,"lines":[" announcements, seed data) must be clearly labeled as such, not presented as if the restaurant"," posted it."," ","-## Confirmed decisions (2026-09-28)","+## Confirmed decisions (2026-09-28, in `/grill-with-docs`)"," ","+- **Site display name is \"La Once Mil\"** — the restaurant's own verified branding.","+  (Corrects the earlier \"Tacos La Oncemil\" spelling used when this brief was started;","+  that was not an intentional name choice. Proceed to `/to-spec`.","originalFile":"# Client brief: Tacos La Oncemil (La Once Mil), Lomas de Chapultepec, Mexico City\n\n## Why this client\n\nI picked this restaurant because the Michelin-star story is compelling: a taqueria — a\ncategory of restaurant normally associated with cheap, fast street food — won a Michelin\nstar in 2026, the only taquería to hold that distinction. That tension (a $20 wagyu taco next\nto a genre built on $1 street tacos) is a strong hook for a \"what can I eat here, where is it,\nwhen is it open\" public site, and the restaurant's real story (chef César de la Parra\ndeliberately elevating a street-food format he grew up on) gives the \"Our Story\" page\nsomething specific to say instead of generic restaurant copy.\n\n**Scope note:** this project models only the flagship location — Monte Everest 780, Lomas\nde Chapultepec — the Michelin-starred address. The restaurant also operates a second Mexico\nCity branch (Roma Norte) and, as of very recently (Sept 2026), a Madrid location; both are\nexplicitly out of scope. See `notes/restaurant-research.md` for full sourcing and the\nnaming decision (site uses \"Tacos La Oncemil,\" the restaurant's own primary branding is \"La\nOnce Mil\" — the two names are used interchangeably in the restaurant's own material).\n\n## Who runs the site, and how comfortable are they with computers?\n\n**Proposed assumption, not a verified fact** (I have not contacted the restaurant): the site\nis modeled as run by the owner, César de la Parra, posting everything himself. He's a working\nchef running a 55-seat, ~80-staff restaurant — comfortable enough to run Instagram and\nTikTok accounts personally, but with no patience for a complicated publishing workflow. He\nneeds to post fast between service, not fight with a CMS. This means the editor UI has to be\nsimple even though, today, there's only one real user.\n\nThe CMS still needs two enforced roles (admin/editor) per the assignment's fixed\nrequirements — the brief models a plausible future where a manager or social-media hire gets\nan editor account without touching user management, menu changes, or the ability to delete\nthe Visit Us / hours information.\n\n## Who reads it, and what are they usually trying to find?\n\nTwo kinds of visitors, inferred from the restaurant's real profile (no reservations, walk-in\nonly, high foot traffic from the Michelin attention, no functioning official website today):\n\n- **First-time visitors drawn by the Michelin coverage**, wanting to know: what's the\n  signature dish, what does it cost, where exactly is it, when is it open, is a reservation\n  needed (no).\n- **Repeat/local visitors** wanting quick answers: today's hours, any seasonal menu news,\n  confirmation the place hasn't moved.\n\n## What's broken about how they do it now?\n\nVerified from research: the restaurant has no functioning official website (`laoncemil.com`\nexists but shows only \"under construction\"). Its entire online presence is Instagram,\nTikTok, and a Linktree — none of which answer \"where and when\" quickly, and all of which bury\nthat information under a scrolling feed. Someone who doesn't already follow the account has\nno fast way to get the address and hours without digging through an Instagram bio.\n\n## What would make them say \"this is better\"?\n\nA page that says, in one glance: what the signature dishes are, that it's walk-in only\n(setting the right expectation before someone shows up expecting to book), the exact address\nand hours, and a way to see it's a real, currently-open, currently-relevant place (recent\nannouncements) without needing to already follow the Instagram.\n\n## What must not happen\n\n**This site must never imply that Tacos La Oncemil / La Once Mil commissioned, endorsed, or\nwas involved in building this project.** It is a student prototype built for a class\nassignment using publicly available, verified information. Any demonstration content (sample\nannouncements, seed data) must be clearly labeled as such, not presented as if the restaurant\nposted it.\n\n## Confirmed decisions (2026-09-28, in `/grill-with-docs`)\n\n- **Site display name is \"La Once Mil\"** — the restaurant's own verified branding.\n  (Corrects the earlier \"Tacos La Oncemil\" spelling used when this brief was started;\n  that was not an intentional name choice. See `notes/restaurant-research.md`.)\n- **Publishing is admin-only.** Only the manager/admin role can publish content live;\n  the demo editor can create and edit announcement drafts but cannot publish, cannot\n  edit permanent pages (Menu, Visit Us/Hours, Our Story), and cannot manage users. The\n  admin can do everything. This is a class prototype modeling a hypothetical future\n  hire, not real restaurant staff.\n- **Demo accounts are fictional, not the real owner.** Seed users are named\n  **\"Demo Manager\"** (admin) and **\"Demo Editor\"** (editor) — required to demonstrate\n  both roles for grading, but explicitly not claiming to be César de la Parra or any\n  real staff member.\n- **Homepage priority order: address, hours, directions first.** Of the \"what/where/when\"\n  facts a first-time visitor needs, address/hours/directions rank above signature-dish\n  or walk-in-only copy on the homepage specifically (those still belong on the page,\n  just not the top fold).\n- **Contact method is phone only.** No contact form, no email address surfaced to\n  customers — a phone number is the one channel offered for reaching the restaurant.\n- **Menu is one ordinary Markdown page** (dish names and descriptions), not a\n  structured menu/pricing database. No unverified peso prices are included, per\n  `notes/restaurant-research.md`'s pricing caveat.\n- **News/announcements may include one real, dated item** — the Michelin star\n  announcement, since the Michelin Guide page directly confirms the exact distinction\n  (\"One MICHELIN Star\") and attributes it to the Lomas de Chapultepec address\n  specifically (see `notes/restaurant-research.md`). Any other seed announcements are\n  invented sample content and must be clearly labeled as demo, not real restaurant\n  posts.\n- **Images: placeholders now, real photos intended for the final version.** Build\n  proceeds today with clearly labeled placeholders (e.g. `[PLACEHOLDER: storefront\n  photo]`) so nothing blocks on photo access. See \"Image tracker\" below for what's\n  still needed before final.\n\n## Image tracker (placeholders in use until these are supplied)\n\n| Needed for | Status | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Homepage hero image | Placeholder | Storefront or signature dish shot, Lomas de Chapultepec location only |\n| Menu page image(s) | Placeholder | Food shots; no prices, per pricing caveat |\n| Our Story image | Placeholder | Chef/kitchen or storefront shot |\n| News/announcement images (optional, per post) | Placeholder | Only if a specific post needs one |\n\nPer `notes/restaurant-research.md`: the three photos found in the Michelin article are\ncredited \"© La Once Mil\" (editorial credit, not a republishing license) and are **not\ncleared for use**. Real photos must come from the user's own Instagram pulls (with\npost date/caption/credit noted) or the user's own photography — not these Michelin\narticle images, and not AI-generated or stock substitutes.\n\n## Still open (proposed requirements to settle in `/grill-with-docs`, not decided here)\n\n- Whether \"Visit Us\" is its own page (separate from the homepage) or folded into Home\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":114,"oldLines":6,"newStart":114,"newLines":14,"lines":[" post date/caption/credit noted) or the user's own photography — not these Michelin"," article images, and not AI-generated or stock substitutes."," ","-## Still open (proposed requirements to settle in `/grill-with-docs`, not decided here)","+- **Home covers visiting information entirely** — verified address, hours, a","+  directions link, and a prominent Call button live on Home itself. This is a class prototype modeling a hypothetical future\n  hire, not real restaurant staff.\n- **Demo accounts are fictional, not the real owner.** Seed users are named\n  **\"Demo Manager\"** (admin) and **\"Demo Editor\"** (editor) — required to demonstrate\n  both roles for grading, but explicitly not claiming to be César de la Parra or any\n  real staff member.\n- **Homepage priority order: address, hours, directions first.** Of the \"what/where/when\"\n  facts a first-time visitor needs, address/hours/directions rank above signature-dish\n  or walk-in-only copy on the homepage specifically (those still belong on the page,\n  just not the top fold).\n- **Contact method is phone only.** No contact form, no email address surfaced to\n  customers — a phone number is the one channel offered for reaching the restaurant.\n- **Menu is one ordinary Markdown page** (dish names and descriptions), not a\n  structured menu/pricing database. No unverified peso prices are included, per\n  `notes/restaurant-research.md`'s pricing caveat.\n- **News/announcements may include one real, dated item** — the Michelin star\n  announcement, since the Michelin Guide page directly confirms the exact distinction\n  (\"One MICHELIN Star\") and attributes it to the Lomas de Chapultepec address\n  specifically (see `notes/restaurant-research.md`). Any other seed announcements are\n  invented sample content and must be clearly labeled as demo, not real restaurant\n  posts.\n- **Images: placeholders now, real photos intended for the final version.** Build\n  proceeds today with clearly labeled placeholders (e.g. `[PLACEHOLDER: storefront\n  photo]`) so nothing blocks on photo access. Real photos must come from the user's own Instagram pulls (with\npost date/caption/credit noted) or the user's own photography — not these Michelin\narticle images, and not AI-generated or stock substitutes.\n\n- **Home covers visiting information entirely** — verified address, hours, a\n  directions link, and a prominent Call button live on Home itself. There is **no\n  separate Visit Us page**; the earlier client-brief assumption of a standalone\n  Visit Us/Hours page is superseded by this decision.\n- **Permanent pages are Home, Menu, and Our Story.** Only the admin can edit them.\n  **News** is the list of published posts (the \"Posts\" capability), which the editor\n  can draft and the admin can publish.\n\n## Still open\n\nNone — `/grill-with-docs` frontier is closed as of 2026-09-28. That tension (a $20 wagyu taco next\n8\tto a genre built on $1 street tacos) is a strong hook for a \"what can I eat here, where is it,\n9\twhen is it open\" public site, and the restaurant's real story (chef César de la Parra\n10\tdeliberately elevating a street-food format he grew up on) gives the \"Our Story\" page\n11\tsomething specific to say instead of generic restaurant copy.\n12\t\n13\t**Scope note:** this project models only the flagship location — Monte Everest 780, Lomas\n14\tde Chapultepec — the Michelin-starred address. He\n26\tneeds to post fast between service, not fight with a CMS. This means the editor UI has to be\n27\tsimple even though, today, there's only one real user.\n28\t\n29\tThe CMS still needs two enforced roles (admin/editor) per the assignment's fixed\n30\trequirements — the brief models a plausible future where a manager or social-media hire gets\n31\tan editor account without touching user management, permanent-page content (Home, Menu, Our\n32\tStory — which includes the address/hours/directions on Home), or publishing.\n33\t\n34\t## Who reads it, and what are they usually trying to find?\n35\t\n36\tTwo kinds of visitors, inferred from the restaurant's real profile (no reservations, walk-in\n37\tonly, high foot traffic from the Michelin attention, no functioning official website today):\n38\t\n39\t- **First-time visitors drawn by the Michelin coverage**, wanting to know: what's the\n40\t  signature dish, what does it cost, where exactly is it, when is it open, is a reservation\n41\t  needed (no).\n42\t- **Repeat/local visitors** wanting quick answers: today's hours, any seasonal menu news,\n43\t  confirmation the place hasn't moved.\n44\t\n45\t## What's broken about how they do it now?\n46\t\n47\tVerified from research: the restaurant has no functioning official website (`laoncemil.com`\n48\texists but shows only \"under construction\"). {"parentUuid":"d7e32807-f181-454b-8836-b99f288abc90","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"add4db92-b3ed-4213-b7fa-c487af583231","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FYBoBdLF5gcF2qpQSr9twM","type":"tool_result","content":"The file /Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/notes/client-brief.md has been updated successfully. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"05da16d2-4dbd-4bca-81dc-43be8ba88a0a","timestamp":"2026-09-29T03:00:08.760Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/notes/client-brief.md","oldString":"# Client brief: Tacos La Oncemil (La Once Mil), Lomas de Chapultepec, Mexico City","newString":"# Client brief: La Once Mil, Lomas de Chapultepec, Mexico City","originalFile":"# Client brief: Tacos La Oncemil (La Once Mil), Lomas de Chapultepec, Mexico City\n\n## Why this client\n\nI picked this restaurant because the Michelin-star story is compelling: a taqueria — a\ncategory of restaurant normally associated with cheap, fast street food — won a Michelin\nstar in 2026, the only taquería to hold that distinction. That tension (a $20 wagyu taco next\nto a genre built on $1 street tacos) is a strong hook for a \"what can I eat here, where is it,\nwhen is it open\" public site, and the restaurant's real story (chef César de la Parra\ndeliberately elevating a street-food format he grew up on) gives the \"Our Story\" page\nsomething specific to say instead of generic restaurant copy.\n\n**Scope note:** this project models only the flagship location — Monte Everest 780, Lomas\nde Chapultepec — the Michelin-starred address. The restaurant also operates a second Mexico\nCity branch (Roma Norte) and, as of very recently (Sept 2026), a Madrid location; both are\nexplicitly out of scope. See `notes/restaurant-research.md` for full sourcing and the\nnaming decision (site uses \"Tacos La Oncemil,\" the restaurant's own primary branding is \"La\nOnce Mil\" — the two names are used interchangeably in the restaurant's own material).\n\n## Who runs the site, and how comfortable are they with computers?\n\n**Proposed assumption, not a verified fact** (I have not contacted the restaurant): the site\nis modeled as run by the owner, César de la Parra, posting everything himself. He's a working\nchef running a 55-seat, ~80-staff restaurant — comfortable enough to run Instagram and\nTikTok accounts personally, but with no patience for a complicated publishing workflow. He\nneeds to post fast between service, not fight with a CMS. This means the editor UI has to be\nsimple even though, today, there's only one real user.\n\nThe CMS still needs two enforced roles (admin/editor) per the assignment's fixed\nrequirements — the brief models a plausible future where a manager or social-media hire gets\nan editor account without touching user management, permanent-page content (Home, Menu, Our\nStory — which includes the address/hours/directions on Home), or publishing.\n\n## Who reads it, and what are they usually trying to find?\n\nTwo kinds of visitors, inferred from the restaurant's real profile (no reservations, walk-in\nonly, high foot traffic from the Michelin attention, no functioning official website today):\n\n- **First-time visitors drawn by the Michelin coverage**, wanting to know: what's the\n  signature dish, what does it cost, where exactly is it, when is it open, is a reservation\n  needed (no).\n- **Repeat/local visitors** wanting quick answers: today's hours, any seasonal menu news,\n  confirmation the place hasn't moved.\n\n## What's broken about how they do it now?\n\nVerified from research: the restaurant has no functioning official website (`laoncemil.com`\nexists but shows only \"under construction\"). Its entire online presence is Instagram,\nTikTok, and a Linktree — none of which answer \"where and when\" quickly, and all of which bury\nthat information under a scrolling feed. Someone who doesn't already follow the account has\nno fast way to get the address and hours without digging through an Instagram bio.\n\n## What would make them say \"this is better\"?\n\nA page that says, in one glance: what the signature dishes are, that it's walk-in only\n(setting the right expectation before someone shows up expecting to book), the exact address\nand hours, and a way to see it's a real, currently-open, currently-relevant place (recent\nannouncements) without needing to already follow the Instagram.\n\n## What must not happen\n\n**This site must never imply that Tacos La Oncemil / La Once Mil commissioned, endorsed, or\nwas involved in building this project.** It is a student prototype built for a class\nassignment using publicly available, verified information. Any demonstration content (sample\nannouncements, seed data) must be clearly labeled as such, not presented as if the restaurant\nposted it.\n\n## Confirmed decisions (2026-09-28, in `/grill-with-docs`)\n\n- **Site display name is \"La Once Mil\"** — the restaurant's own verified branding.\n  (Corrects the earlier \"Tacos La Oncemil\" spelling used when this brief was started;\n  that was not an intentional name choice. See `notes/restaurant-research.md`.)\n- **Publishing is admin-only.** Only the manager/admin role can publish content live;\n  the demo editor can create and edit announcement drafts but cannot publish, cannot\n  edit permanent pages (Menu, Visit Us/Hours, Our Story), and cannot manage users. The\n  admin can do everything. This is a class prototype modeling a hypothetical future\n  hire, not real restaurant staff.\n- **Demo accounts are fictional, not the real owner.** Seed users are named\n  **\"Demo Manager\"** (admin) and **\"Demo Editor\"** (editor) — required to demonstrate\n  both roles for grading, but explicitly not claiming to be César de la Parra or any\n  real staff member.\n- **Homepage priority order: address, hours, directions first.** Of the \"what/where/when\"\n  facts a first-time visitor needs, address/hours/directions rank above signature-dish\n  or walk-in-only copy on the homepage specifically (those still belong on the page,\n  just not the top fold).\n- **Contact method is phone only.** No contact form, no email address surfaced to\n  customers — a phone number is the one channel offered for reaching the restaurant.\n- **Menu is one ordinary Markdown page** (dish names and descriptions), not a\n  structured menu/pricing database. No unverified peso prices are included, per\n  `notes/restaurant-research.md`'s pricing caveat.\n- **News/announcements may include one real, dated item** — the Michelin star\n  announcement, since the Michelin Guide page directly confirms the exact distinction\n  (\"One MICHELIN Star\") and attributes it to the Lomas de Chapultepec address\n  specifically (see `notes/restaurant-research.md`). Any other seed announcements are\n  invented sample content and must be clearly labeled as demo, not real restaurant\n  posts.\n- **Images: placeholders now, real photos intended for the final version.** Build\n  proceeds today with clearly labeled placeholders (e.g. `[PLACEHOLDER: storefront\n  photo]`) so nothing blocks on photo access. See \"Image tracker\" below for what's\n  still needed before final.\n\n## Image tracker (placeholders in use until these are supplied)\n\n| Needed for | Status | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Homepage hero image | Placeholder | Storefront or signature dish shot, Lomas de Chapultepec location only |\n| Menu page image(s) | Placeholder | Food shots; no prices, per pricing caveat |\n| Our Story image | Placeholder | Chef/kitchen or storefront shot |\n| News/announcement images (optional, per post) | Placeholder | Only if a specific post needs one |\n\nPer `notes/restaurant-research.md`: the three photos found in the Michelin article are\ncredited \"© La Once Mil\" (editorial credit, not a republishing license) and are **not\ncleared for use**. Real photos must come from the user's own Instagram pulls (with\npost date/caption/credit noted) or the user's own photography — not these Michelin\narticle images, and not AI-generated or stock substitutes.\n\n- **Home covers visiting information entirely** — verified address, hours, a\n  directions link, and a prominent Call button live on Home itself. The restaurant also operates a second Mexico\nCity branch (Roma Norte) and, as of very recently (Sept 2026), a Madrid location; both are\nexplicitly out of scope. See `notes/restaurant-research.md` for full sourcing and the\nnaming decision (site uses \"La Once Mil,\" the restaurant's own verified branding; an\nearlier draft of this brief used \"Tacos La Oncemil,\" which was corrected on 2026-09-28).","originalFile":"# Client brief: La Once Mil, Lomas de Chapultepec, Mexico City\n\n## Why this client\n\nI picked this restaurant because the Michelin-star story is compelling: a taqueria — a\ncategory of restaurant normally associated with cheap, fast street food — won a Michelin\nstar in 2026, the only taquería to hold that distinction. That tension (a $20 wagyu taco next\nto a genre built on $1 street tacos) is a strong hook for a \"what can I eat here, where is it,\nwhen is it open\" public site, and the restaurant's real story (chef César de la Parra\ndeliberately elevating a street-food format he grew up on) gives the \"Our Story\" page\nsomething specific to say instead of generic restaurant copy.\n\n**Scope note:** this project models only the flagship location — Monte Everest 780, Lomas\nde Chapultepec — the Michelin-starred address. The restaurant also operates a second Mexico\nCity branch (Roma Norte) and, as of very recently (Sept 2026), a Madrid location; both are\nexplicitly out of scope. See `notes/restaurant-research.md` for full sourcing and the\nnaming decision (site uses \"Tacos La Oncemil,\" the restaurant's own primary branding is \"La\nOnce Mil\" — the two names are used interchangeably in the restaurant's own material).\n\n## Who runs the site, and how comfortable are they with computers?\n\n**Proposed assumption, not a verified fact** (I have not contacted the restaurant): the site\nis modeled as run by the owner, César de la Parra, posting everything himself. He's a working\nchef running a 55-seat, ~80-staff restaurant — comfortable enough to run Instagram and\nTikTok accounts personally, but with no patience for a complicated publishing workflow. He\nneeds to post fast between service, not fight with a CMS. This means the editor UI has to be\nsimple even though, today, there's only one real user.\n\nThe CMS still needs two enforced roles (admin/editor) per the assignment's fixed\nrequirements — the brief models a plausible future where a manager or social-media hire gets\nan editor account without touching user management, permanent-page content (Home, Menu, Our\nStory — which includes the address/hours/directions on Home), or publishing.\n\n## Who reads it, and what are they usually trying to find?\n\nTwo kinds of visitors, inferred from the restaurant's real profile (no reservations, walk-in\nonly, high foot traffic from the Michelin attention, no functioning official website today):\n\n- **First-time visitors drawn by the Michelin coverage**, wanting to know: what's the\n  signature dish, what does it cost, where exactly is it, when is it open, is a reservation\n  needed (no).\n- **Repeat/local visitors** wanting quick answers: today's hours, any seasonal menu news,\n  confirmation the place hasn't moved.\n\n## What's broken about how they do it now?\n\nVerified from research: the restaurant has no functioning official website (`laoncemil.com`\nexists but shows only \"under construction\"). Its entire online presence is Instagram,\nTikTok, and a Linktree — none of which answer \"where and when\" quickly, and all of which bury\nthat information under a scrolling feed. Someone who doesn't already follow the account has\nno fast way to get the address and hours without digging through an Instagram bio.\n\n## What would make them say \"this is better\"?\n\nA page that says, in one glance: what the signature dishes are, that it's walk-in only\n(setting the right expectation before someone shows up expecting to book), the exact address\nand hours, and a way to see it's a real, currently-open, currently-relevant place (recent\nannouncements) without needing to already follow the Instagram.\n\n## What must not happen\n\n**This site must never imply that Tacos La Oncemil / La Once Mil commissioned, endorsed, or\nwas involved in building this project.** It is a student prototype built for a class\nassignment using publicly available, verified information. Any demonstration content (sample\nannouncements, seed data) must be clearly labeled as such, not presented as if the restaurant\nposted it.\n\n## Confirmed decisions (2026-09-28, in `/grill-with-docs`)\n\n- **Site display name is \"La Once Mil\"** — the restaurant's own verified branding.\n  (Corrects the earlier \"Tacos La Oncemil\" spelling used when this brief was started;\n  that was not an intentional name choice. See `notes/restaurant-research.md`.)\n- **Publishing is admin-only.** Only the manager/admin role can publish content live;\n  the demo editor can create and edit announcement drafts but cannot publish, cannot\n  edit permanent pages (Menu, Visit Us/Hours, Our Story), and cannot manage users. The\n  admin can do everything. This is a class prototype modeling a hypothetical future\n  hire, not real restaurant staff.\n- **Demo accounts are fictional, not the real owner.** Seed users are named\n  **\"Demo Manager\"** (admin) and **\"Demo Editor\"** (editor) — required to demonstrate\n  both roles for grading, but explicitly not claiming to be César de la Parra or any\n  real staff member.\n- **Homepage priority order: address, hours, directions first.** Of the \"what/where/when\"\n  facts a first-time visitor needs, address/hours/directions rank above signature-dish\n  or walk-in-only copy on the homepage specifically (those still belong on the page,\n  just not the top fold).\n- **Contact method is phone only.** No contact form, no email address surfaced to\n  customers — a phone number is the one channel offered for reaching the restaurant.\n- **Menu is one ordinary Markdown page** (dish names and descriptions), not a\n  structured menu/pricing database. No unverified peso prices are included, per\n  `notes/restaurant-research.md`'s pricing caveat.\n- **News/announcements may include one real, dated item** — the Michelin star\n  announcement, since the Michelin Guide page directly confirms the exact distinction\n  (\"One MICHELIN Star\") and attributes it to the Lomas de Chapultepec address\n  specifically (see `notes/restaurant-research.md`). Any other seed announcements are\n  invented sample content and must be clearly labeled as demo, not real restaurant\n  posts.\n- **Images: placeholders now, real photos intended for the final version.** Build\n  proceeds today with clearly labeled placeholders (e.g. `[PLACEHOLDER: storefront\n  photo]`) so nothing blocks on photo access. See \"Image tracker\" below for what's\n  still needed before final.\n\n## Image tracker (placeholders in use until these are supplied)\n\n| Needed for | Status | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Homepage hero image | Placeholder | Storefront or signature dish shot, Lomas de Chapultepec location only |\n| Menu page image(s) | Placeholder | Food shots; no prices, per pricing caveat |\n| Our Story image | Placeholder | Chef/kitchen or storefront shot |\n| News/announcement images (optional, per post) | Placeholder | Only if a specific post needs one |\n\nPer `notes/restaurant-research.md`: the three photos found in the Michelin article are\ncredited \"© La Once Mil\" (editorial credit, not a republishing license) and are **not\ncleared for use**. Real photos must come from the user's own Instagram pulls (with\npost date/caption/credit noted) or the user's own photography — not these Michelin\narticle images, and not AI-generated or stock substitutes.\n\n- **Home covers visiting information entirely** — verified address, hours, a\n  directions link, and a prominent Call button live on Home itself. There is **no\n  separate Visit Us page**; the earlier client-brief assumption of a standalone\n  Visit Us/Hours page is superseded by this decision.\n- **Permanent pages are Home, Menu, and Our Story.** Only the admin can edit them.\n  **News** is the list of published posts (the \"Posts\" capability), which the editor\n  can draft and the admin can publish.\n\n## Still open\n\nNone — `/grill-with-docs` frontier is closed as of 2026-09-28. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"c93e0907-f176-4387-a07b-17c29e7e9d70","timestamp":"2026-09-29T03:00:21.850Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/notes/client-brief.md","oldString":"article images, and not AI-generated or stock substitutes.\n\n- **Home covers visiting information entirely** — verified address, hours, a\n  directions link, and a prominent Call button live on Home itself. There is **no\n  separate Visit Us page**; the earlier client-brief assumption of a standalone\n  Visit Us/Hours page is superseded by this decision.\n- **Permanent pages are Home, Menu, and Our Story.** Only the admin can edit them.\n  **News** is the list of published posts (the \"Posts\" capability), which the editor\n  can draft and the admin can publish.\n\n## Still open","newString":"article images, and not AI-generated or stock substitutes.\n\n## Page structure (2026-09-28, in `/grill-with-docs`)\n\n- **Home covers visiting information entirely** — verified address, hours, a\n  directions link, and a prominent Call button live on Home itself. There is **no\n  separate Visit Us page**; the earlier assumption elsewhere in this brief of a\n  standalone Visit Us/Hours page is superseded by this decision.\n- **Permanent pages are Home, Menu, and Our Story.** Only the admin can edit them.\n  **News** is the list of published posts (the \"Posts\" capability), which the editor\n  can draft and the admin can publish.\n- **Publishing marks content published in the local CMS only.** The public GitHub\n  Pages site does not update automatically — it reflects the new state only after\n  `cms publish` exports to `site/` and that export is deployed to Pages. \"Published\"\n  and \"live on the public site\" are two different moments.\n- **Every published page, including Home, must be reachable through navigation.**\n  Home is the entry point rather than a separate nav link, but Menu, Our Story, and\n  News must all be linked from it (and from each other) so no published content is\n  an orphan page.\n\n## Still open","originalFile":"# Client brief: La Once Mil, Lomas de Chapultepec, Mexico City\n\n## Why this client\n\nI picked this restaurant because the Michelin-star story is compelling: a taqueria — a\ncategory of restaurant normally associated with cheap, fast street food — won a Michelin\nstar in 2026, the only taquería to hold that distinction. That tension (a $20 wagyu taco next\nto a genre built on $1 street tacos) is a strong hook for a \"what can I eat here, where is it,\nwhen is it open\" public site, and the restaurant's real story (chef César de la Parra\ndeliberately elevating a street-food format he grew up on) gives the \"Our Story\" page\nsomething specific to say instead of generic restaurant copy.\n\n**Scope note:** this project models only the flagship location — Monte Everest 780, Lomas\nde Chapultepec — the Michelin-starred address. The restaurant also operates a second Mexico\nCity branch (Roma Norte) and, as of very recently (Sept 2026), a Madrid location; both are\nexplicitly out of scope. See `notes/restaurant-research.md` for full sourcing and the\nnaming decision (site uses \"La Once Mil,\" the restaurant's own verified branding; an\nearlier draft of this brief used \"Tacos La Oncemil,\" which was corrected on 2026-09-28).\n\n## Who runs the site, and how comfortable are they with computers?\n\n**Proposed assumption, not a verified fact** (I have not contacted the restaurant): the site\nis modeled as run by the owner, César de la Parra, posting everything himself. He's a working\nchef running a 55-seat, ~80-staff restaurant — comfortable enough to run Instagram and\nTikTok accounts personally, but with no patience for a complicated publishing workflow. He\nneeds to post fast between service, not fight with a CMS. This means the editor UI has to be\nsimple even though, today, there's only one real user.\n\nThe CMS still needs two enforced roles (admin/editor) per the assignment's fixed\nrequirements — the brief models a plausible future where a manager or social-media hire gets\nan editor account without touching user management, permanent-page content (Home, Menu, Our\nStory — which includes the address/hours/directions on Home), or publishing.\n\n## Who reads it, and what are they usually trying to find?\n\nTwo kinds of visitors, inferred from the restaurant's real profile (no reservations, walk-in\nonly, high foot traffic from the Michelin attention, no functioning official website today):\n\n- **First-time visitors drawn by the Michelin coverage**, wanting to know: what's the\n  signature dish, what does it cost, where exactly is it, when is it open, is a reservation\n  needed (no).\n- **Repeat/local visitors** wanting quick answers: today's hours, any seasonal menu news,\n  confirmation the place hasn't moved.\n\n## What's broken about how they do it now?\n\nVerified from research: the restaurant has no functioning official website (`laoncemil.com`\nexists but shows only \"under construction\"). Its entire online presence is Instagram,\nTikTok, and a Linktree — none of which answer \"where and when\" quickly, and all of which bury\nthat information under a scrolling feed. Someone who doesn't already follow the account has\nno fast way to get the address and hours without digging through an Instagram bio.\n\n## What would make them say \"this is better\"?\n\nA page that says, in one glance: what the signature dishes are, that it's walk-in only\n(setting the right expectation before someone shows up expecting to book), the exact address\nand hours, and a way to see it's a real, currently-open, currently-relevant place (recent\nannouncements) without needing to already follow the Instagram.\n\n## What must not happen\n\n**This site must never imply that Tacos La Oncemil / La Once Mil commissioned, endorsed, or\nwas involved in building this project.** It is a student prototype built for a class\nassignment using publicly available, verified information. Any demonstration content (sample\nannouncements, seed data) must be clearly labeled as such, not presented as if the restaurant\nposted it.\n\n## Confirmed decisions (2026-09-28, in `/grill-with-docs`)\n\n- **Site display name is \"La Once Mil\"** — the restaurant's own verified branding.\n  (Corrects the earlier \"Tacos La Oncemil\" spelling used when this brief was started;\n  that was not an intentional name choice. See `notes/restaurant-research.md`.)\n- **Publishing is admin-only.** Only the manager/admin role can publish content live;\n  the demo editor can create and edit announcement drafts but cannot publish, cannot\n  edit permanent pages (Home, Menu, Our Story), and cannot manage users. The\n  admin can do everything. This is a class prototype modeling a hypothetical future\n  hire, not real restaurant staff.\n- **Demo accounts are fictional, not the real owner.** Seed users are named\n  **\"Demo Manager\"** (admin) and **\"Demo Editor\"** (editor) — required to demonstrate\n  both roles for grading, but explicitly not claiming to be César de la Parra or any\n  real staff member.\n- **Homepage priority order: address, hours, directions first.** Of the \"what/where/when\"\n  facts a first-time visitor needs, address/hours/directions rank above signature-dish\n  or walk-in-only copy on the homepage specifically (those still belong on the page,\n  just not the top fold).\n- **Contact method is phone only.** No contact form, no email address surfaced to\n  customers — a phone number is the one channel offered for reaching the restaurant.\n- **Menu is one ordinary Markdown page** (dish names and descriptions), not a\n  structured menu/pricing database. No unverified peso prices are included, per\n  `notes/restaurant-research.md`'s pricing caveat.\n- **News/announcements may include one real, dated item** — the Michelin star\n  announcement, since the Michelin Guide page directly confirms the exact distinction\n  (\"One MICHELIN Star\") and attributes it to the Lomas de Chapultepec address\n  specifically (see `notes/restaurant-research.md`). Any other seed announcements are\n  invented sample content and must be clearly labeled as demo, not real restaurant\n  posts.\n- **Images: placeholders now, real photos intended for the final version.** Build\n  proceeds today with clearly labeled placeholders (e.g. `[PLACEHOLDER: storefront\n  photo]`) so nothing blocks on photo access. See \"Image tracker\" below for what's\n  still needed before final.\n\n## Image tracker (placeholders in use until these are supplied)\n\n| Needed for | Status | Notes |\n|---|---|---|\n| Homepage hero image | Placeholder | Storefront or signature dish shot, Lomas de Chapultepec location only |\n| Menu page image(s) | Placeholder | Food shots; no prices, per pricing caveat |\n| Our Story image | Placeholder | Chef/kitchen or storefront shot |\n| News/announcement images (optional, per post) | Placeholder | Only if a specific post needs one |\n\nPer `notes/restaurant-research.md`: the three photos found in the Michelin article are\ncredited \"© La Once Mil\" (editorial credit, not a republishing license) and are **not\ncleared for use**. Real photos must come from the user's own Instagram pulls (with\npost date/caption/credit noted) or the user's own photography — not these Michelin\narticle images, and not AI-generated or stock substitutes.\n\n- **Home covers visiting information entirely** — verified address, hours, a\n  directions link, and a prominent Call button live on Home itself. There is **no\n  separate Visit Us page**; the earlier client-brief assumption of a standalone\n  Visit Us/Hours page is superseded by this decision.\n- **Permanent pages are Home, Menu, and Our Story.** Only the admin can edit them.\n  **News** is the list of published posts (the \"Posts\" capability), which the editor\n  can draft and the admin can publish.\n\n## Still open\n\nNone — `/grill-with-docs` frontier is closed as of 2026-09-28. Supersedes the earlier \"Tacos La Oncemil\" spelling used before this session, which was not an intentional name choice. |\n| **Flagship location** | The one restaurant location this project models: Monte Everest 780, Lomas de Chapultepec, Mexico City — the Michelin-starred address. Editor drafts; admin publishes. |\n| **Publish** | The admin-only action that moves a draft (News post or, implicitly, a permanent page edit) to live/public. Tracked in `notes/client-brief.md`'s image tracker. As a mobile bank customer, I want to see balance on my accounts, so that I can make better informed decisions about my spending\n</user-story-example>\n\nThis list of user stories should be extremely extensive and cover all aspects of the feature.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\nA list of implementation decisions that were made. {"parentUuid":"2ce43dee-0dfc-4e02-af82-93ddabfbcd20","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"f13f457b-8615-4eaf-95a0-a539b4153851","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_015gtDrC177qBJCXH6YxxEdQ","type":"tool_result","content":"# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.\n- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.\n- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.\n- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body \"<answer>\"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.\n===domain===\n# Domain Docs\n\nHow the engineering skills should consume this repo's domain documentation when exploring the codebase.\n\n## Before exploring, read these\n\n- **`CONTEXT.md`** at the repo root, or\n- **`CONTEXT-MAP.md`** at the repo root if it exists: it points at one `CONTEXT.md` per context. Read each one relevant to the topic.\n- **`docs/adr/`**: read ADRs that touch the area you're about to work in. In multi-context repos, also check `src/<context>/docs/adr/` for context-scoped decisions.\n\nIf any of these files don't exist, **proceed silently**. Don't flag their absence; don't suggest creating them upfront. The `/domain-modeling` skill (reached via `/grill-with-docs` and `/improve-codebase-architecture`) creates them lazily when terms or decisions actually get resolved.\n\n## File structure\n\nThis repo is single-context:\n\n```\n/\n├── CONTEXT.md\n├── docs/adr/\n│   ├── ADR-001-local-admin-static-public.md\n│   └── ADR-002-stack.md\n└── app/\n```\n\n## Use the glossary's vocabulary\n\nWhen your output names a domain concept (in an issue title, a refactor proposal, a hypothesis, a test name), use the term as defined in `CONTEXT.md`. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.\n- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.\n- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.\n- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body \"<answer>\"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.\n===domain===\n# Domain Docs\n\nHow the engineering skills should consume this repo's domain documentation when exploring the codebase.\n\n## Before exploring, read these\n\n- **`CONTEXT.md`** at the repo root, or\n- **`CONTEXT-MAP.md`** at the repo root if it exists: it points at one `CONTEXT.md` per context. {"parentUuid":"40f07143-df26-4db2-ad53-7e084c9f9cb6","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"f13f457b-8615-4eaf-95a0-a539b4153851","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_019owPRR6myg1oojm1T5S3t3","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"The `cms` command: serve, publish, deploy.\n2\t\n3\t    uv run cms serve      # admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\n4\t    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\n5\t    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\n6\t\"\"\"\n7\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n8\t\n9\timport argparse\n10\timport subprocess\n11\timport sys\n12\t\n13\tfrom app import settings\n14\tfrom app.publish import render_site\n15\t\n16\t\n17\tdef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n18\t    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n19\t    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n20\t    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n21\t    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n22\t    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n23\t    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n24\t    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n25\t    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n26\t    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n27\t\n28\t    if args.command == \"serve\":\n29\t        import uvicorn\n30\t\n31\t        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", port=args.port, reload=args.reload)\n32\t        return 0\n33\t\n34\t    if args.command == \"publish\":\n35\t        out = render_site()\n36\t        print(f\"Wrote {out}. Preview it with:  python3 -m http.server -d {out} 8001\")\n37\t        return 0\n38\t\n39\t    if args.command == \"deploy\":\n40\t        if not settings.SITE.exists():\n41\t            print(\"site/ does not exist yet — run `uv run cms publish` first.\")\n42\t            return 1\n43\t        result = subprocess.run(\n44\t            [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"ghp_import\", \"-n\", \"-p\", \"-m\", args.message,\n45\t             str(settings.SITE)],\n46\t        )\n47\t        if result.returncode == 0:\n48\t            print(\"Pushed to gh-pages. Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> \"\n49\t                  \"gh-pages / root, then wait up to 10 minutes.\")\n50\t        return result.returncode\n51\t    return 1\n52\t\n53\t\n54\tif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n55\t    raise SystemExit(main())\n56\t"}]},"uuid":"c1c1cea6-6f46-450d-a2d6-2c5e5f51a53f","timestamp":"2026-09-29T03:01:05.745Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/cli.py","content":"\"\"\"The `cms` command: serve, publish, deploy.\n\n    uv run cms serve      # admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\n    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\n    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.command == \"serve\":\n        import uvicorn\n\n        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", port=args.port, reload=args.reload)\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"publish\":\n        out = render_site()\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. {"parentUuid":"2dcf5f87-89bb-4479-ad63-d01ec52b0698","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"f13f457b-8615-4eaf-95a0-a539b4153851","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01GyhHBqz9niRHpqXfqQjp6V","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# ADR-001: The admin console runs locally; the public site is a static export\n2\t\n3\t**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n4\t**Date:** 2026-09-22\n5\t\n6\t## Context\n7\t\n8\tA CMS needs a server, a database, and login. GitHub Pages serves static files\n9\tonly: it cannot run Python and has no database. Students have two weeks and no\n10\thosting budget, and a first web application with real authentication is an\n11\tattractive target the moment it is public.\n12\t\n13\t## Decision\n14\t\n15\tThe admin console (FastAPI + SQLite) runs on the student's own machine. A\n16\t`cms publish` step renders the published content to static HTML in `site/`, which\n17\tis deployed to GitHub Pages on the `gh-pages` branch.\n18\t\n19\t## Consequences\n20\t\n21\t- Login, roles, and the database are never exposed to the internet.\n22\t- The public site cannot have server-side features (search, comments) without a\n23\t  different host; a stretch goal may add a live admin deploy behind a security gate.\n24\t- Publishing is explicit: content changes are not live until `cms publish` runs,\n25\t  which is a behaviour worth documenting for your client.\n26\t- Relative paths become mandatory, because Pages serves the site from a subfolder.\n27\t\n28\t## Why this is an ADR\n29\t\n30\tIt is hard to reverse (it shapes every route, template, and deploy step) and it\n31\tis surprising without context (most CMSes are servers). That is the bar; most\n32\tdecisions do not meet it and belong in the spec or the glossary instead.\n33\t"}]},"uuid":"7364df18-75a3-40f0-80ba-a634481f7afa","timestamp":"2026-09-29T03:01:07.272Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-001-local-admin-static-public.md","content":"# ADR-001: The admin console runs locally; the public site is a static export\n\n**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n**Date:** 2026-09-22\n\n## Context\n\nA CMS needs a server, a database, and login. GitHub Pages serves static files\nonly: it cannot run Python and has no database. Students have two weeks and no\nhosting budget, and a first web application with real authentication is an\nattractive target the moment it is public.\n\n## Decision\n\nThe admin console (FastAPI + SQLite) runs on the student's own machine. A\n`cms publish` step renders the published content to static HTML in `site/`, which\nis deployed to GitHub Pages on the `gh-pages` branch.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Login, roles, and the database are never exposed to the internet.\n- The public site cannot have server-side features (search, comments) without a\n  different host; a stretch goal may add a live admin deploy behind a security gate.\n- Publishing is explicit: content changes are not live until `cms publish` runs,\n  which is a behaviour worth documenting for your client.\n- Relative paths become mandatory, because Pages serves the site from a subfolder.\n\n## Why this is an ADR\n\nIt is hard to reverse (it shapes every route, template, and deploy step) and it\nis surprising without context (most CMSes are servers). That is the bar; most\ndecisions do not meet it and belong in the spec or the glossary instead.\n","numLines":33,"startLine":1,"totalLines":33}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"2dcf5f87-89bb-4479-ad63-d01ec52b0698","session_id":"a2316d11-3941-4d87-98fe-7d21dea1d9fa","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6f927223-ede7-411f-b8cf-dcb15a4b0a35","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"92bac9f4-5345-4c83-b221-5a9832a61a9f","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"f13f457b-8615-4eaf-95a0-a539b4153851","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01H5qye8DGJ4kpmCUwVUsX8u","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# ADR-002: FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, with no frontend framework\n2\t\n3\t**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n4\t**Date:** 2026-09-22\n5\t\n6\t## Context\n7\t\n8\tThe project has to be readable by someone who has never built a web application,\n9\tgradable from a clean clone, and finishable in two weeks on a $20 plan. Options\n10\tconsidered: Django (batteries included, but a large amount of generated code to\n11\tread), Flask (similar to FastAPI here), a JavaScript stack (a second language and\n12\ta build step), and FastAPI with server-rendered templates.\n13\t\n14\t## Decision\n15\t\n16\tFastAPI with Jinja2 templates, SQLite for storage, argon2 for password hashing,\n17\tand an HTML sanitizer for user Markdown. No frontend framework, no build step.\n18\t\n19\t## Consequences\n20\t\n21\t- Every page is server-rendered, so \"view source\" shows what the code produced,\n22\t  which makes debugging visible.\n23\t- SQLite is a single file, so a grader can seed and inspect it easily. It is\n24\t  gitignored; `scripts/seed_demo.py` rebuilds it.\n25\t- No build step means the file you preview is the file that ships.\n26\t- Interactive flourishes (live preview without reload, drag-and-drop) cost more\n27\t  here than in a JavaScript stack. That is an accepted trade.\n28\t"}]},"uuid":"6d45fbe9-f33a-452b-89f3-c5aa63e02eeb","timestamp":"2026-09-29T03:01:07.757Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-002-stack.md","content":"# ADR-002: FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, with no frontend framework\n\n**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n**Date:** 2026-09-22\n\n## Context\n\nThe project has to be readable by someone who has never built a web application,\ngradable from a clean clone, and finishable in two weeks on a $20 plan. Options\nconsidered: Django (batteries included, but a large amount of generated code to\nread), Flask (similar to FastAPI here), a JavaScript stack (a second language and\na build step), and FastAPI with server-rendered templates.\n\n## Decision\n\nFastAPI with Jinja2 templates, SQLite for storage, argon2 for password hashing,\nand an HTML sanitizer for user Markdown. No frontend framework, no build step.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Every page is server-rendered, so \"view source\" shows what the code produced,\n  which makes debugging visible.\n- SQLite is a single file, so a grader can seed and inspect it easily. Passwords come from the environment there; in\n18\t# tests they are fixed and meaningless.\n19\tDEMO_USERS = {\n20\t    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"admin@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n21\t    \"editor\": {\"email\": \"editor@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n22\t}\n23\t\n24\t\n25\t@pytest.fixture\n26\tdef client() -> TestClient:\n27\t    return TestClient(create_app())\n28\t\n29\t\n30\t@pytest.fixture\n31\tdef client_as():\n32\t    \"\"\"Return a factory: client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n33\t\n34\t    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n35\t        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n36\t        c = TestClient(create_app())\n37\t        response = c.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": user[\"email\"],\n38\t                                          \"password\": user[\"password\"]},\n39\t                          follow_redirects=False)\n40\t        if response.status_code == 404:\n41\t            pytest.skip(\"No /login route yet — build the login ticket first.\")\n42\t        assert response.status_code in (200, 302, 303), (\n43\t            f\"Login as {role} failed with {response.status_code}\")\n44\t        return c\n45\t\n46\t    return _login\n47\t"}]},"uuid":"d9857ddf-8846-4978-90dc-b1c5d0a3f342","timestamp":"2026-09-29T03:01:10.705Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/tests/conftest.py","content":"\"\"\"Shared test fixtures.\n\n`client` gives you the app. `client_as(role)` gives you a client that is logged\nin as a seeded user of that role — it works as soon as your login route exists,\nso access-control tests stay one line:\n\n    def test_editor_cannot_manage_users(client_as):\n        assert client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin/users\").status_code in (302, 403)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app.main import create_app\n\n# Matches scripts/seed_demo.py. Passwords come from the environment there; in\n# tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"admin@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"email\": \"editor@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n}\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client() -> TestClient:\n    return TestClient(create_app())\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client_as():\n    \"\"\"Return a factory: client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n\n    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n        c = TestClient(create_app())\n        response = c.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": user[\"email\"],\n                                          \"password\": user[\"password\"]},\n                          follow_redirects=False)\n        if response.status_code == 404:\n            pytest.skip(\"No /login route yet — build the login ticket first.\")\n        assert response.status_code in (200, 302, 303), (\n            f\"Login as {role} failed with {response.status_code}\")\n        return c\n\n    return _login\n","numLines":47,"startLine":1,"totalLines":47}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"d33fb78f-2204-4913-87a3-5128568ac0c9","session_id":"a2316d11-3941-4d87-98fe-7d21dea1d9fa","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6f927223-ede7-411f-b8cf-dcb15a4b0a35","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"main"}

This is already built and is the natural highest seam — tests hit routes and assert on responses/redirects, never touching the DB or template internals directly.\n2. **`render_site()` in `app/publish.py`** — the seam for the publish/export behavior: only published content reaches `site/`, relative paths only, Home/Menu/Our Story/News all linked.
