{"parentUuid":"19c15f13-a257-46a1-ac05-39a031f19e33","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfWzDmPvMhDhraUvkJUj5","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"thinking","thinking":"","signature":""}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":145,"cache_read_input_tokens":137986,"output_tokens":5695,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":125},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":145,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":5695,"cache_read_input_tokens":137986,"cache_creation_input_tokens":145,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":145},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"ecdce33e-e1be-41cf-b320-abfc1692bef0","apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011CfWzDkxdTGY58JbPd4ztK","type":"assistant","uuid":"20e4c2d6-cb3c-4061-8938-dc1b6227980c","timestamp":"2026-09-29T03:03:03.333Z","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":null,"session_id":"a2316d11-3941-4d87-98fe-7d21dea1d9fa","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6f927223-ede7-411f-b8cf-dcb15a4b0a35","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"main"}
{"parentUuid":"20e4c2d6-cb3c-4061-8938-dc1b6227980c","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfWzDmPvMhDhraUvkJUj5","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_013X4NoK5icB4kZxJmTZFyGw","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-alejandrogonzalez-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/6f927223-ede7-411f-b8cf-dcb15a4b0a35/scratchpad/spec.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nLa Once Mil (the Michelin-starred flagship taquería at Monte Everest 780, Lomas de\nChapultepec, Mexico City) has no usable web presence. Its official domain\n(`laoncemil.com`) is a permanent \"under construction\" page, and its real online\npresence — Instagram, TikTok, a Linktree — buries the one thing most visitors need\n(address, hours, \"is it walk-in only\") under a scrolling feed. A first-time visitor\ndrawn by Michelin coverage, or a repeat local visitor checking today's hours, has no\nfast way to get that information without digging through a social feed they may not\nalready follow. There is also no simple way for the restaurant to post a dated\nannouncement (e.g. news, seasonal changes) without it disappearing into that same feed.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS with a local admin console (never exposed to the internet, per ADR-001)\nand a static public site exported to GitHub Pages. The public Home page leads with\nverified address, hours, a directions link, and a prominent Call button, because that\nis the one glance a visitor needs. A Manager role can publish News, edit the\npermanent pages (Home, Menu, Our Story), and manage user accounts; an Editor role can\ndraft News for the Manager to review and publish, but cannot publish anything, edit\nthe permanent pages, or touch user accounts. Publishing marks content as published in\nthe local CMS only — the public GitHub Pages site reflects that change only after\n`cms publish` exports to `site/` and that export is deployed.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As the Manager, I want to log in with a hashed password, so that only I can reach\n   the admin console.\n2. As the Manager, I want to log out, so that a shared or public machine doesn't stay\n   signed in.\n3. As anyone entering a wrong password, I want a clear rejection message with no\n   account created or session started, so that login failures are unambiguous.\n4. As the Editor, I want to log in with my own hashed-password account, so that I can\n   draft News without sharing the Manager's credentials.\n5. As an anonymous visitor, I want to be redirected to login when I try to reach any\n   admin route, so that the admin console is never reachable without authentication.\n6. As the Manager, I want the Editor's role to visibly differ from mine (different\n   nav options, different available actions), so that the two roles are genuinely\n   distinct, not just a label.\n7. As the Editor, I want to be blocked (403 or redirect, never a silent no-op) if I\n   submit a direct HTTP request to a Manager-only route (publish, permanent-page edit,\n   user management) even without using the UI, so that the restriction can't be\n   bypassed by hand-crafting a request.\n8. As the Manager, I want to create, edit, and delete News posts (title, slug,\n   Markdown body, draft/published status, author, timestamps), so that I can keep the\n   public site current.\n9. As the Editor, I want to create and edit News posts as drafts, so that I can\n   prepare an announcement for the Manager's review.\n10. As the Editor, I want my save actions to always leave the post in draft status\n    (never published), so that I cannot accidentally or deliberately publish content.\n11. As the Manager, I want to publish or unpublish a News post, so that I control what\n    reaches the public site.\n12. As the Manager, I want the News list to be filterable by status (draft/published),\n    so that I can find what still needs review.\n13. As the Manager, I want to edit the Home, Menu, and Our Story pages (each with\n    title, slug, Markdown body, draft/published status, author, timestamps, matching\n    the Posts capability's fields), so that I control the site's permanent content.\n14. As the Editor, I want the permanent-page editors to be unreachable to me (no UI\n    entry point, and a 403/redirect if I try the route directly), so that the\n    \"Editor never touches permanent pages\" rule is enforced, not just hidden.\n15. As a visitor, I want a published permanent page to appear in the public site's\n    navigation once it's exported, so that I can reach Menu and Our Story from Home.\n16. As the Manager, I want a dashboard that shows counts of News posts (draft vs.\n    published) and permanent-page status, so that I can see the site's state at a\n    glance.\n17. As the Manager, I want a content list I can filter by type (News/Pages) and by\n    status, so that I can navigate a growing set of content without scrolling\n    everything.\n18. As the Manager or Editor, I want a Markdown preview in the editor before saving,\n    so that I can see how the rendered content will look.\n19. As the Manager, I want to create a new user account (email, password, role), so\n    that I can add an Editor when needed.\n20. As the Manager, I want to change a user's role, so that I can promote or demote\n    without deleting and recreating the account.\n21. As the Manager, I want to deactivate a user, so that someone who shouldn't have\n    access anymore loses it without deleting their historical authorship record.\n22. As a deactivated user, I want my login attempt to be refused with a clear message,\n    even with the correct password, so that deactivation is actually enforced.\n23. As the Editor, I want the user-management routes to be unreachable to me (no UI\n    entry point, and a 403/redirect on direct request), so that only the Manager\n    controls accounts.\n24. As a visitor, I want the public Home page to show verified address, hours, a\n    directions link, and a prominent Call button, prioritized above other content\n    (signature dish, walk-in-only note), so that I get the \"where and when\" answer\n    immediately.\n25. As a visitor, I want the public site to show only published content — no draft\n    ever appears — so that I never see unfinished or unreviewed material.\n26. As a visitor, I want any Markdown-authored content (News, Home, Menu, Our Story)\n    to render safely, with scripts and dangerous attributes stripped, so that the\n    public site can't be used to inject malicious content even if a draft author\n    pasted something unsafe.\n27. As a visitor, I want every link and asset on the exported site to use a relative\n    path (never root-absolute), so that the site works correctly when served from a\n    GitHub Pages project subfolder.\n28. As a visitor, I want every published page — including Home — reachable by\n    clicking through the site's navigation, so that no published content is an\n    unlinked orphan.\n29. As the Manager, I want `cms publish` to regenerate `site/` from only the current\n    published content, so that unpublishing something and re-running publish actually\n    removes it from the export.\n30. As the Manager, I want a News post to include one real, dated Michelin star\n    announcement (attributed to the Lomas de Chapultepec address, matching the\n    Michelin Guide's own attribution) alongside clearly labeled demo announcements, so\n    that the demo doesn't read as entirely fictional while staying honest about what's\n    invented.\n31. As anyone viewing any seed/demo content, I want a clear label distinguishing real,\n    sourced content from invented sample content, so that the site never implies La\n    Once Mil created or endorsed this project.\n32. As the grader/developer, I want two seeded demo accounts (\"Demo Manager\",\n    \"Demo Editor\") that are clearly fictional and not tied to the real owner's\n    identity, so that both roles are testable without misrepresenting real staff.\n33. As the Manager, I want the Menu page to be one ordinary Markdown page listing dish\n    names and descriptions with no prices, so that I never publish an unverified peso\n    price.\n34. As a visitor, I want image placeholders (e.g. `[PLACEHOLDER: storefront photo]`)\n    to render as clearly labeled placeholders rather than broken image tags, so that\n    missing photography doesn't look like a bug.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Roles**: two enforced roles, `admin` (\"Manager\" in client-facing copy) and\n  `editor`. Role is a column on the user record, checked server-side on every\n  state-changing and every admin-only read route — never enforced only by hiding UI.\n- **Permission matrix**:\n  - `admin`: create/edit/delete/publish News; create/edit permanent pages (Home,\n    Menu, Our Story); create/edit-role/deactivate users; view dashboard and full\n    content list.\n  - `editor`: create/edit News as drafts only (cannot set status to published, cannot\n    delete a published post); cannot reach permanent-page editors or user-management\n    routes (403/redirect on both UI and direct request); can view the dashboard and\n    content list scoped to what they're allowed to act on.\n- **Content types**: `Post` (News) and `Page` (Home, Menu, Our Story) share the same\n  field set — title, slug, Markdown body, status (`draft`/`published`), author\n  (foreign key to user), created/updated timestamps. `Page` additionally participates\n  in the public navigation once published; `Post` (News) is listed reverse-chronological\n  on a News index.\n- **Permanent pages are fixed, not freely creatable**: exactly three Page records\n  (Home, Menu, Our Story) exist for this client — creating a fourth arbitrary Page is\n  out of scope (see Out of Scope). Home is not a nav entry itself (it's the entry\n  point); Menu and Our Story are.\n- **Publish/export boundary (ADR-001)**: \"published\" is a status flag in the local\n  SQLite database — it does not touch the public site. `cms publish` (via\n  `render_site()` in `app/publish.py`) reads only `status = published` rows, renders\n  Markdown through the sanitizer, and writes `site/` with one file per published item\n  plus a News index and nav links built from published Pages. `cms deploy` pushes\n  `site/` to `gh-pages`. These are three distinct moments (publish-in-CMS, export,\n  deploy) and the spec never conflates them.\n- **Sanitization**: Markdown bodies are converted with `markdown-it-py` then passed\n  through `nh3` (already a pinned dependency) before being written to `site/` or\n  rendered in the admin preview — both surfaces sanitize, not just the export.\n- **Sessions**: signed session cookies (`itsdangerous`, already pinned) carrying user\n  id and role; no client-side role trust — every request re-checks role from the\n  session-resolved user record so a deactivated user's existing session stops working\n  on the next request, not just at next login.\n- **Password storage**: argon2 (`argon2-cffi`, already pinned) hashes only; plaintext\n  is never stored or logged.\n- **CSRF**: every state-changing form (login excluded, since it has no prior session)\n  carries a CSRF token validated server-side before the action runs.\n- **Deactivation**: a boolean/status flag on the user record. Deactivated users fail\n  login with a clear rejection message even with the correct password, and any\n  existing session for that user is treated as invalid on the next authenticated\n  request.\n- **Seed data** (`scripts/seed_demo.py`): creates exactly two users, \"Demo Manager\"\n  (admin) and \"Demo Editor\" (editor), with passwords read from the environment\n  (`.env.example` documents the variable names) — never hard-coded, never the real\n  owner's name. Seeds the three permanent pages (Home/Menu/Our Story, published) and\n  a small set of News posts: one real dated item (the Michelin star announcement,\n  attributed to the Lomas de Chapultepec address) plus additional clearly-labeled\n  demo announcements (e.g. a `[DEMO CONTENT]` marker in the body or a dedicated\n  \"demo\" flag rendered as a badge).\n- **Images**: no upload/media-library feature in this spec (that's the \"Media uploads\"\n  stretch goal). Placeholder images are literal labeled text/markup\n  (`[PLACEHOLDER: storefront photo]`) embedded in seed content, rendered as visible\n  placeholder blocks, not broken `<img>` tags.\n- **Modules to build** (new, under `app/`): `app/models.py` or `app/db.py` (SQLite\n  schema: users, pages, posts), `app/auth.py` (login/session/CSRF/role-check\n  helpers), `app/routes/auth.py`, `app/routes/posts.py`, `app/routes/pages.py`,\n  `app/routes/users.py`, `app/routes/admin.py` (dashboard/content list), each\n  `include_router`'d from `app/main.py` per its existing comment. `app/publish.py`\n  extends `render_site()` to iterate published Posts/Pages instead of the current\n  hard-coded empty-items placeholder.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- Tests only assert on external behavior — HTTP status/redirect/response body for the\n  HTTP seam, and files/content under `site/` for the export seam. Problem Statement\n\nLa Once Mil (the Michelin-starred flagship taquería at Monte Everest 780, Lomas de\nChapultepec, Mexico City) has no usable web presence. Its official domain\n(`laoncemil.com`) is a permanent \"under construction\" page, and its real online\npresence — Instagram, TikTok, a Linktree — buries the one thing most visitors need\n(address, hours, \"is it walk-in only\") under a scrolling feed. A first-time visitor\ndrawn by Michelin coverage, or a repeat local visitor checking today's hours, has no\nfast way to get that information without digging through a social feed they may not\nalready follow. There is also no simple way for the restaurant to post a dated\nannouncement (e.g. news, seasonal changes) without it disappearing into that same feed.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS with a local admin console (never exposed to the internet, per ADR-001)\nand a static public site exported to GitHub Pages. The public Home page leads with\nverified address, hours, a directions link, and a prominent Call button, because that\nis the one glance a visitor needs. A Manager role can publish News, edit the\npermanent pages (Home, Menu, Our Story), and manage user accounts; an Editor role can\ndraft News for the Manager to review and publish, but cannot publish anything, edit\nthe permanent pages, or touch user accounts. Publishing marks content as published in\nthe local CMS only — the public GitHub Pages site reflects that change only after\n`cms publish` exports to `site/` and that export is deployed.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As the Manager, I want to log in with a hashed password, so that only I can reach\n   the admin console.\n2. As the Manager, I want to log out, so that a shared or public machine doesn't stay\n   signed in.\n3. As anyone entering a wrong password, I want a clear rejection message with no\n   account created or session started, so that login failures are unambiguous.\n4. As the Editor, I want to log in with my own hashed-password account, so that I can\n   draft News without sharing the Manager's credentials.\n5. As an anonymous visitor, I want to be redirected to login when I try to reach any\n   admin route, so that the admin console is never reachable without authentication.\n6. As the Manager, I want the Editor's role to visibly differ from mine (different\n   nav options, different available actions), so that the two roles are genuinely\n   distinct, not just a label.\n7. As the Editor, I want to be blocked (403 or redirect, never a silent no-op) if I\n   submit a direct HTTP request to a Manager-only route (publish, permanent-page edit,\n   user management) even without using the UI, so that the restriction can't be\n   bypassed by hand-crafting a request.\n8. As the Manager, I want to create, edit, and delete News posts (title, slug,\n   Markdown body, draft/published status, author, timestamps), so that I can keep the\n   public site current.\n9. As the Editor, I want to create and edit News posts as drafts, so that I can\n   prepare an announcement for the Manager's review.\n10. As the Editor, I want my save actions to always leave the post in draft status\n    (never published), so that I cannot accidentally or deliberately publish content.\n11. As the Manager, I want to publish or unpublish a News post, so that I control what\n    reaches the public site.\n12. As the Manager, I want the News list to be filterable by status (draft/published),\n    so that I can find what still needs review.\n13. As the Manager, I want to edit the Home, Menu, and Our Story pages (each with\n    title, slug, Markdown body, draft/published status, author, timestamps, matching\n    the Posts capability's fields), so that I control the site's permanent content.\n14. As the Editor, I want the permanent-page editors to be unreachable to me (no UI\n    entry point, and a 403/redirect if I try the route directly), so that the\n    \"Editor never touches permanent pages\" rule is enforced, not just hidden.\n15. As a visitor, I want a published permanent page to appear in the public site's\n    navigation once it's exported, so that I can reach Menu and Our Story from Home.\n16. As the Manager, I want a dashboard that shows counts of News posts (draft vs.\n    published) and permanent-page status, so that I can see the site's state at a\n    glance.\n17. As the Manager, I want a content list I can filter by type (News/Pages) and by\n    status, so that I can navigate a growing set of content without scrolling\n    everything.\n18. As the Manager or Editor, I want a Markdown preview in the editor before saving,\n    so that I can see how the rendered content will look.\n19. As the Manager, I want to create a new user account (email, password, role), so\n    that I can add an Editor when needed.\n20. As the Manager, I want to change a user's role, so that I can promote or demote\n    without deleting and recreating the account.\n21. As the Manager, I want to deactivate a user, so that someone who shouldn't have\n    access anymore loses it without deleting their historical authorship record.\n22. As a deactivated user, I want my login attempt to be refused with a clear message,\n    even with the correct password, so that deactivation is actually enforced.\n23. As the Editor, I want the user-management routes to be unreachable to me (no UI\n    entry point, and a 403/redirect on direct request), so that only the Manager\n    controls accounts.\n24. As a visitor, I want the public Home page to show verified address, hours, a\n    directions link, and a prominent Call button, prioritized above other content\n    (signature dish, walk-in-only note), so that I get the \"where and when\" answer\n    immediately.\n25. As a visitor, I want the public site to show only published content — no draft\n    ever appears — so that I never see unfinished or unreviewed material.\n26. As a visitor, I want any Markdown-authored content (News, Home, Menu, Our Story)\n    to render safely, with scripts and dangerous attributes stripped, so that the\n    public site can't be used to inject malicious content even if a draft author\n    pasted something unsafe.\n27. As a visitor, I want every link and asset on the exported site to use a relative\n    path (never root-absolute), so that the site works correctly when served from a\n    GitHub Pages project subfolder.\n28. As a visitor, I want every published page — including Home — reachable by\n    clicking through the site's navigation, so that no published content is an\n    unlinked orphan.\n29. As the Manager, I want `cms publish` to regenerate `site/` from only the current\n    published content, so that unpublishing something and re-running publish actually\n    removes it from the export.\n30. As the Manager, I want a News post to include one real, dated Michelin star\n    announcement (attributed to the Lomas de Chapultepec address, matching the\n    Michelin Guide's own attribution) alongside clearly labeled demo announcements, so\n    that the demo doesn't read as entirely fictional while staying honest about what's\n    invented.\n31. As anyone viewing any seed/demo content, I want a clear label distinguishing real,\n    sourced content from invented sample content, so that the site never implies La\n    Once Mil created or endorsed this project.\n32. As the grader/developer, I want two seeded demo accounts (\"Demo Manager\",\n    \"Demo Editor\") that are clearly fictional and not tied to the real owner's\n    identity, so that both roles are testable without misrepresenting real staff.\n33. As the Manager, I want the Menu page to be one ordinary Markdown page listing dish\n    names and descriptions with no prices, so that I never publish an unverified peso\n    price.\n34. As a visitor, I want image placeholders (e.g. `[PLACEHOLDER: storefront photo]`)\n    to render as clearly labeled placeholders rather than broken image tags, so that\n    missing photography doesn't look like a bug.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Roles**: two enforced roles, `admin` (\"Manager\" in client-facing copy) and\n  `editor`. Role is a column on the user record, checked server-side on every\n  state-changing and every admin-only read route — never enforced only by hiding UI.\n- **Permission matrix**:\n  - `admin`: create/edit/delete/publish News; create/edit permanent pages (Home,\n    Menu, Our Story); create/edit-role/deactivate users; view dashboard and full\n    content list.\n  - `editor`: create/edit News as drafts only (cannot set status to published, cannot\n    delete a published post); cannot reach permanent-page editors or user-management\n    routes (403/redirect on both UI and direct request); can view the dashboard and\n    content list scoped to what they're allowed to act on.\n- **Content types**: `Post` (News) and `Page` (Home, Menu, Our Story) share the same\n  field set — title, slug, Markdown body, status (`draft`/`published`), author\n  (foreign key to user), created/updated timestamps. `Page` additionally participates\n  in the public navigation once published; `Post` (News) is listed reverse-chronological\n  on a News index.\n- **Permanent pages are fixed, not freely creatable**: exactly three Page records\n  (Home, Menu, Our Story) exist for this client — creating a fourth arbitrary Page is\n  out of scope (see Out of Scope). Home is not a nav entry itself (it's the entry\n  point); Menu and Our Story are.\n- **Publish/export boundary (ADR-001)**: \"published\" is a status flag in the local\n  SQLite database — it does not touch the public site. `cms publish` (via\n  `render_site()` in `app/publish.py`) reads only `status = published` rows, renders\n  Markdown through the sanitizer, and writes `site/` with one file per published item\n  plus a News index and nav links built from published Pages. `cms deploy` pushes\n  `site/` to `gh-pages`. These are three distinct moments (publish-in-CMS, export,\n  deploy) and the spec never conflates them.\n- **Sanitization**: Markdown bodies are converted with `markdown-it-py` then passed\n  through `nh3` (already a pinned dependency) before being written to `site/` or\n  rendered in the admin preview — both surfaces sanitize, not just the export.\n- **Sessions**: signed session cookies (`itsdangerous`, already pinned) carrying user\n  id and role; no client-side role trust — every request re-checks role from the\n  session-resolved user record so a deactivated user's existing session stops working\n  on the next request, not just at next login.\n- **Password storage**: argon2 (`argon2-cffi`, already pinned) hashes only; plaintext\n  is never stored or logged.\n- **CSRF**: every state-changing form (login excluded, since it has no prior session)\n  carries a CSRF token validated server-side before the action runs.\n- **Deactivation**: a boolean/status flag on the user record. Deactivated users fail\n  login with a clear rejection message even with the correct password, and any\n  existing session for that user is treated as invalid on the next authenticated\n  request.\n- **Seed data** (`scripts/seed_demo.py`): creates exactly two users, \"Demo Manager\"\n  (admin) and \"Demo Editor\" (editor), with passwords read from the environment\n  (`.env.example` documents the variable names) — never hard-coded, never the real\n  owner's name. Seeds the three permanent pages (Home/Menu/Our Story, published) and\n  a small set of News posts: one real dated item (the Michelin star announcement,\n  attributed to the Lomas de Chapultepec address) plus additional clearly-labeled\n  demo announcements (e.g. a `[DEMO CONTENT]` marker in the body or a dedicated\n  \"demo\" flag rendered as a badge).\n- **Images**: no upload/media-library feature in this spec (that's the \"Media uploads\"\n  stretch goal). Placeholder images are literal labeled text/markup\n  (`[PLACEHOLDER: storefront photo]`) embedded in seed content, rendered as visible\n  placeholder blocks, not broken `<img>` tags.\n- **Modules to build** (new, under `app/`): `app/models.py` or `app/db.py` (SQLite\n  schema: users, pages, posts), `app/auth.py` (login/session/CSRF/role-check\n  helpers), `app/routes/auth.py`, `app/routes/posts.py`, `app/routes/pages.py`,\n  `app/routes/users.py`, `app/routes/admin.py` (dashboard/content list), each\n  `include_router`'d from `app/main.py` per its existing comment. `app/publish.py`\n  extends `render_site()` to iterate published Posts/Pages instead of the current\n  hard-coded empty-items placeholder.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- Tests only assert on external behavior — HTTP status/redirect/response body for the\n  HTTP seam, and files/content under `site/` for the export seam. No test reaches into\n  the database or calls an internal function to check state a real user/visitor\n  couldn't observe.\n- **Seam 1 — HTTP** (`client`, `client_as` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py`,\n  prior art: `tests/test_t00.py`): login success/failure/logout; anonymous access to\n  any admin route redirects to login; `client_as(\"editor\")` gets 403/redirect on\n  every admin-only route (permanent-page edit, publish action, user management) —\n  including a direct POST that bypasses the UI entirely, matching the \"editors cannot\n  bypass restrictions by submitting requests directly\" requirement; Editor CRUD on\n  News is confined to draft status; Manager can publish/unpublish; dashboard and\n  content-list filters return the expected counts/subsets; user creation, role\n  change, and deactivation each work only for the admin client; a deactivated user's\n  login is refused and, if feasible to simulate, their existing session stops\n  authenticating on the next request.\n- **Seam 2 — Export** (`render_site()` in `app/publish.py`, prior art:\n  `tests/test_t00.py`'s two existing publish tests): a draft never appears in any file\n  under `site/`; a `<script>`/`onerror=` payload saved in a post's body does not\n  survive into the exported HTML unescaped/executable; every `href=`/`src=` in the\n  exported output is relative, never root-absolute; Home, Menu, Our Story, and the\n  News index are all reachable by following links present in the exported HTML\n  (no orphan published page); unpublishing an item and re-running `render_site()`\n As a visitor, I want any Markdown-authored content (News, Home, Menu, Our Story)\n    to render safely, with scripts and dangerous attributes stripped, so that the\n    public site can't be used to inject malicious content even if a draft author\n    pasted something unsafe.\n27. As a visitor, I want every link and asset on the exported site to use a relative\n    path (never root-absolute), so that the site works correctly when served from a\n    GitHub Pages project subfolder.\n28. As a visitor, I want every published page — including Home — reachable by\n    clicking through the site's navigation, so that no published content is an\n    unlinked orphan.\n29. As the Manager, I want `cms publish` to regenerate `site/` from only the current\n    published content, so that unpublishing something and re-running publish actually\n    removes it from the export.\n30. As the Manager, I want a News post to include one real, dated Michelin star\n    announcement (attributed to the Lomas de Chapultepec address, matching the\n    Michelin Guide's own attribution) alongside clearly labeled demo announcements, so\n    that the demo doesn't read as entirely fictional while staying honest about what's\n    invented.\n31. As anyone viewing any seed/demo content, I want a clear label distinguishing real,\n    sourced content from invented sample content, so that the site never implies La\n    Once Mil created or endorsed this project.\n32. As the grader/developer, I want two seeded demo accounts (\"Demo Manager\",\n    \"Demo Editor\") that are clearly fictional and not tied to the real owner's\n    identity, so that both roles are testable without misrepresenting real staff.\n33. As the Manager, I want the Menu page to be one ordinary Markdown page listing dish\n    names and descriptions with no prices, so that I never publish an unverified peso\n    price.\n34. As a visitor, I want image placeholders (e.g. `[PLACEHOLDER: storefront photo]`)\n    to render as clearly labeled placeholders rather than broken image tags, so that\n    missing photography doesn't look like a bug.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n- **Roles**: two enforced roles, `admin` (\"Manager\" in client-facing copy) and\n  `editor`. Role is a column on the user record, checked server-side on every\n  state-changing and every admin-only read route — never enforced only by hiding UI.\n- **Permission matrix**:\n  - `admin`: create/edit/delete/publish News; create/edit permanent pages (Home,\n    Menu, Our Story); create/edit-role/deactivate users; view dashboard and full\n    content list.\n  - `editor`: create/edit News as drafts only (cannot set status to published, cannot\n    delete a published post); cannot reach permanent-page editors or user-management\n    routes (403/redirect on both UI and direct request); can view the dashboard and\n    content list scoped to what they're allowed to act on.\n- **Content types**: `Post` (News) and `Page` (Home, Menu, Our Story) share the same\n  field set — title, slug, Markdown body, status (`draft`/`published`), author\n  (foreign key to user), created/updated timestamps. `Page` additionally participates\n  in the public navigation once published; `Post` (News) is listed reverse-chronological\n  on a News index.\n- **Permanent pages are fixed, not freely creatable**: exactly three Page records\n  (Home, Menu, Our Story) exist for this client — creating a fourth arbitrary Page is\n  out of scope (see Out of Scope). Home is not a nav entry itself (it's the entry\n  point); Menu and Our Story are.\n- **Publish/export boundary (ADR-001)**: \"published\" is a status flag in the local\n  SQLite database — it does not touch the public site. `cms publish` (via\n  `render_site()` in `app/publish.py`) reads only `status = published` rows, renders\n  Markdown through the sanitizer, and writes `site/` with one file per published item\n  plus a News index and nav links built from published Pages. `cms deploy` pushes\n  `site/` to `gh-pages`. These are three distinct moments (publish-in-CMS, export,\n  deploy) and the spec never conflates them.\n- **Sanitization**: Markdown bodies are converted with `markdown-it-py` then passed\n  through `nh3` (already a pinned dependency) before being written to `site/` or\n  rendered in the admin preview — both surfaces sanitize, not just the export.\n- **Sessions**: signed session cookies (`itsdangerous`, already pinned) carrying user\n  id and role; no client-side role trust — every request re-checks role from the\n  session-resolved user record so a deactivated user's existing session stops working\n  on the next request, not just at next login.\n- **Password storage**: argon2 (`argon2-cffi`, already pinned) hashes only; plaintext\n  is never stored or logged.\n- **CSRF**: every state-changing form (login excluded, since it has no prior session)\n  carries a CSRF token validated server-side before the action runs.\n- **Deactivation**: a boolean/status flag on the user record. Deactivated users fail\n  login with a clear rejection message even with the correct password, and any\n  existing session for that user is treated as invalid on the next authenticated\n  request.\n- **Seed data** (`scripts/seed_demo.py`): creates exactly two users, \"Demo Manager\"\n  (admin) and \"Demo Editor\" (editor), with passwords read from the environment\n  (`.env.example` documents the variable names) — never hard-coded, never the real\n  owner's name. Seeds the three permanent pages (Home/Menu/Our Story, published) and\n  a small set of News posts: one real dated item (the Michelin star announcement,\n  attributed to the Lomas de Chapultepec address) plus additional clearly-labeled\n  demo announcements (e.g. a `[DEMO CONTENT]` marker in the body or a dedicated\n  \"demo\" flag rendered as a badge).\n- **Images**: no upload/media-library feature in this spec (that's the \"Media uploads\"\n  stretch goal). Placeholder images are literal labeled text/markup\n  (`[PLACEHOLDER: storefront photo]`) embedded in seed content, rendered as visible\n  placeholder blocks, not broken `<img>` tags.\n- **Modules to build** (new, under `app/`): `app/models.py` or `app/db.py` (SQLite\n  schema: users, pages, posts), `app/auth.py` (login/session/CSRF/role-check\n  helpers), `app/routes/auth.py`, `app/routes/posts.py`, `app/routes/pages.py`,\n  `app/routes/users.py`, `app/routes/admin.py` (dashboard/content list), each\n  `include_router`'d from `app/main.py` per its existing comment. `app/publish.py`\n  extends `render_site()` to iterate published Posts/Pages instead of the current\n  hard-coded empty-items placeholder.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- Tests only assert on external behavior — HTTP status/redirect/response body for the\n  HTTP seam, and files/content under `site/` for the export seam. No test reaches into\n  the database or calls an internal function to check state a real user/visitor\n  couldn't observe.\n- **Seam 1 — HTTP** (`client`, `client_as` fixtures in `tests/conftest.py`,\n  prior art: `tests/test_t00.py`): login success/failure/logout; anonymous access to\n  any admin route redirects to login; `client_as(\"editor\")` gets 403/redirect on\n  every admin-only route (permanent-page edit, publish action, user management) —\n  including a direct POST that bypasses the UI entirely, matching the \"editors cannot\n  bypass restrictions by submitting requests directly\" requirement; Editor CRUD on\n  News is confined to draft status; Manager can publish/unpublish; dashboard and\n  content-list filters return the expected counts/subsets; user creation, role\n  change, and deactivation each work only for the admin client; a deactivated user's\n  login is refused and, if feasible to simulate, their existing session stops\n  authenticating on the next request.\n- **Seam 2 — Export** (`render_site()` in `app/publish.py`, prior art:\n  `tests/test_t00.py`'s two existing publish tests): a draft never appears in any file\n  under `site/`; a `<script>`/`onerror=` payload saved in a post's body does not\n  survive into the exported HTML unescaped/executable; every `href=`/`src=` in the\n  exported output is relative, never root-absolute; Home, Menu, Our Story, and the\n  News index are all reachable by following links present in the exported HTML\n  (no orphan published page); unpublishing an item and re-running `render_site()`\n  removes it from the output.\n- No new test seam is introduced — both existing fixtures/functions are extended, not\n  replaced.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Contact form or any customer-facing email address (phone only, per client brief).\n- A separate \"Visit Us\" page — visiting information lives entirely on Home.\n- Structured menu/pricing data or any peso prices (no verified pricing exists).\n- Media upload / image library UI (stretch goal, not this spec).\n- User self-registration — only the Manager creates accounts.\n- Any content for the Roma Norte or Madrid locations.\n- Multi-site support, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text WYSIWYG editors (manual's\n  explicit exclusions).\n- Arbitrary/creatable Pages beyond the fixed three (Home, Menu, Our Story).\n- Live admin deploy to the public internet (ADR-001: admin stays local).\n- Revision history, scheduled publishing, comments, search, categories/tags, plugin\n  system — all separate stretch goals, not required here.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- This spec covers all 7 required capabilities from the manual: Login (stories 1–5),\n  Roles (6–7, 14, 23), Posts/News (8–12, 30–31), Pages (13–15, 33), Admin console\n  (16–18), User management (19–23), Public site & publish (24–29, 34).\n- The Editor-cannot-bypass-via-direct-request requirement (explicitly called out by\n  the user) is tested at the HTTP seam by issuing the restricted request directly\n  with `client_as(\"editor\")`, not by only checking that a UI link is hidden.\n- Ticket slicing (next step, `/to-tickets`) should keep each ticket a vertical {"parentUuid":"48fb8676-1b6a-4039-90b7-b51ef922109f","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"060fd5e3-f11f-48bb-bd5f-b4f23f327666","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/alejandrogonzalez/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/to-tickets\n\n# To Tickets\n\nBreak a plan, spec, or conversation into a set of **tickets**: tracer-bullet vertical slices, each declaring the tickets that **block** it.\n\nThe issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Gather context\n\nWork from whatever is already in the conversation context. If the user passes a reference (a spec path, an issue number or URL) as an argument, fetch it and read its full body and comments.\n\n### 2. Explore the codebase (optional)\n\nIf you have not already explored the codebase, do so to understand the current state of the code. Ticket titles and descriptions should use the project's domain glossary vocabulary, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\nLook for opportunities to prefactor the code to make the implementation easier. \"Make the change easy, then make the easy change.\"\n\n### 3. Draft vertical slices\n\nBreak the work into **tracer bullet** tickets.\n\n<vertical-slice-rules>\n\n- Each slice cuts a narrow but COMPLETE path through every layer (schema, API, UI, tests): vertical, NOT a horizontal slice of one layer\n- A completed slice is demoable or verifiable on its own\n- Each slice is sized to fit in a single fresh context window\n- Any prefactoring should be done first\n\n</vertical-slice-rules>\n\nGive each ticket its **blocking edges**: the other tickets that must complete before it can start. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.\n\n**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change (rename a column, retype a shared symbol) whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket; green is promised only there.\n\n### 4. Quiz the user\n\nPresent the proposed breakdown as a numbered list. For each ticket, show:\n\n- **Title**: short descriptive name\n- **Blocked by**: which other tickets (if any) must complete first\n- **What it delivers**: the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work\n\nAsk the user:\n\n- Does the granularity feel right? (too coarse / too fine)\n- Are the blocking edges correct: does each ticket only depend on tickets that genuinely gate it?\n- Should any tickets be merged or split further?\n\nIterate until the user approves the breakdown.\n\n### 5. Publish the tickets to the configured tracker\n\nPublish the approved tickets. **How** depends on the tracker `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` configured; the tickets are the same either way, only the shape of the blocking edges changes:\n\n- **Local files** → write one file per ticket under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01` in dependency order (blockers first). Each file's \"Blocked by\" lists the numbers/titles it depends on. Use the per-ticket file template below: one ticket per file, never a single combined file.\n- **A real issue tracker (GitHub, Linear, …)** → publish one issue per ticket in dependency order (blockers first) so each ticket's blocking edges can reference real identifiers. Use the platform's native blocking / sub-issue relationship where it has one; otherwise set each ticket's \"Blocked by\" to the blocking issues. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label unless instructed otherwise; the tickets are agent-grabbable by construction.\n\nWork the **frontier**: any ticket whose blockers are all done. For a purely linear chain that means top to bottom.\n\nDo NOT close or modify any parent issue.\n\n<local-ticket-template>\n\n# <NN>: <Ticket title>\n\n**What to build:** the end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not a layer-by-layer implementation list.\n\n**Blocked by:** the numbers/titles of the tickets that gate this one, or \"None (can start immediately)\".\n\n**Status:** ready-for-agent\n\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 1\n- [ ] Acceptance criterion 2\n\n</local-ticket-template>\n\n<issue-template>\n\n## Parent\n\nA reference to the parent issue on the tracker (if the source was an existing issue, otherwise omit this section).\n\n## What to build\n\nThe end-to-end behaviour this ticket makes work, from the user's perspective, not layer-by-layer implementation.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Criterion 1\n- [ ] Criterion 2\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- A reference to each blocking ticket, or \"None (can start immediately)\".\n\n</issue-template>\n\nIn either form, avoid specific file paths or code snippets: they go stale fast. Exception: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts, not a working demo, just the important bits.\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"395ee897-ca9c-4aa0-97e1-e3025928370e","timestamp":"2026-09-29T03:06:49.432Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/alejandrogonzalez/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"6f927223-ede7-411f-b8cf-dcb15a4b0a35","version":"2.1.280","gitBranch":"main"}

Parent\n\nSpec: #1\n\n## What to build\n\nEvery state-changing admin form across the whole app rejects a POST without a valid\nCSRF token, and one enumerated test sweep confirms the Editor is blocked — by direct\nrequest, not just a hidden UI link — on every admin-only route that exists once\nT02–T06 have landed, closing any gap an individual ticket's own tests didn't already\ncover.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] Every state-changing form (pages, posts, users — login already covered in T01)\n      rejects a POST with a missing or invalid CSRF token.\n- [ ] A single parametrized test enumerates every admin-only route in the app and\n      asserts the Editor gets 403/redirect on each, via a direct request.\n- [ ] The same enumeration asserts an anonymous visitor is redirected {"parentUuid":"1429a07b-324d-4769-9a91-d063c4efead0","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5","id":"msg_011CfWzkJdicPyo9Nmod3VR3","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"All 7 tickets are created with both a \"Blocked by\" line in the body and native GitHub issue dependencies.\n\n| # | Title | Blocked by | Order |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| [#2](https://github.com/algoal0507-crypto/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/2) T01 | Login and sessions | None | 1 |\n| [#3](https://github.com/algoal0507-crypto/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/3) T02 | Permanent pages (Home, Menu, Our Story) | #2 | 2 |\n| [#4](https://github.com/algoal0507-crypto/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/4) T03 | Publish pipeline and first live deploy | #3 | 3 |\n| [#5](https://github.com/algoal0507-crypto/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/5) T04 | News posts (Editor drafts, Manager publish) | #2, #4 | 4 |\n| [#6](https://github.com/algoal0507-crypto/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/6) T05 | Admin dashboard and filterable content list | #3, #5 | 5 |\n| [#7](https://github.com/algoal0507-crypto/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/7) T06 | User management | #2 | 6 (can run parallel to T04/T05) |\n| [#8](https://github.com/algoal0507-crypto/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/8) T07 | Access-control and CSRF hardening pass | #3, #5, #6, #7 | 7 (last) |\n\n**Stage 1's first three: #2 → #3 → #4.**\n\n**What you'll be able to see after those three:** you'll be able to log in locally as **Demo Manager** or **Demo Editor**, log out, and get a clear rejection on a wrong password. Running `cms publish` then `cms deploy` will produce a real GitHub Pages URL over HTTPS serving that published Home page, with only relative links, satisfying the Stage 1 \"live on Pages\" requirement.
